entry.title: Update goreleaser/goreleaser-action action to v7 (#1395)
entry.content:
Update goreleaser/goreleaser-action action to v7 (#1395)

* Update goreleaser/goreleaser-action action to v7

* ci: pin GoReleaser to v2.9.0 and update configs to version 2

goreleaser-action v7 resolves `version: latest` to GoReleaser v2, where
v5 resolved it to v1. `goreleaser check` on v2.19.0 exits 2 because the
config uses deprecated properties.

- Add `version: 2` and rename `archives.format` to `formats`.
- In .goreleaser-patch.yml, rename `brews.tap` to `repository` and
  `brews.folder` to `directory`; GoReleaser v2 removed the old names.
- Pin GoReleaser to v2.9.0, the last release before `brews` was
  deprecated in favor of `homebrew_casks`. Moving to casks changes how
  the Homebrew tap is published, so it is left for a separate change.

* ci: cap Renovate's GoReleaser updates below v2.10.0

Renovate updates the goreleaser-action `version` input, so it would bump
the v2.9.0 pin to the latest v2 release, which fails `goreleaser check`
on the deprecated `brews` section. Remove the cap after moving to
`homebrew_casks`.

entry.title: feat: warn when src-cli is older than the instance's recommended vers…
entry.content:
feat: warn when src-cli is older than the instance's recommended version (#1403)

* feat: warn when src-cli is older than the instance's recommended version

Before running a command, src does a best-effort check of the running version against the version recommended by the configured instance (/.api/src-cli/version) and prints a single stderr warning when behind. Fail-open, 3s timeout, stderr only so --json is unaffected. Skips version/help/no-arg, dev builds, and SRC_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK. Compares major/minor/patch only. Adds unit tests. Closes #930. Supersedes #1339, #1343.

* fix: make the outdated-version warning safe to ship

- Fix a nil pointer panic on every command in release builds: the check
  built its API client from a zero-value api.Flags.
- Run the check after flags and config are resolved, so -endpoint and
  -config are honored and the right instance is asked.
- Ask the instance at most once every 24 hours per endpoint, caching the
  answer, including a failed lookup, under the user cache directory, so
  an instance that does not answer cannot delay every command.
- Compare versions with Masterminds/semver, which is already linked into
  the binary, instead of a hand-written parser.
- Skip 'src version' by its parsed subcommand instead of scanning every
  argument for the word.
- Test the check end to end against a fake instance.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1c29c-9f51-7761-a4ba-4d4f46dcd4ef
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

* fix: run the version check with the command's own API client

The check ran before the subcommand's flags were parsed, so it ignored
-insecure-skip-verify and never warned on instances with an untrusted
certificate. It also ran twice for nested legacy commands such as
'src repos list', which printed the warning twice.

Run it once per process from config.apiClient instead, using the client
the command asked for. Commands that never talk to the instance, such as
'src search -h', no longer trigger a lookup.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1c29c-9f51-7761-a4ba-4d4f46dcd4ef
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

* docs: document the outdated-version warning and SRC_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK

* feat: make 'src version' warn too, and refresh the cached version

'src version' was the one command that never warned. It now prints the
warning from the answer it just got from the instance, and caches that
answer, so the commands that follow warn about the same version.

It still makes a single request, and 'src version -client-only' still
makes none: the check that other commands get from config.apiClient
keeps skipping 'src version'.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1c29c-9f51-7761-a4ba-4d4f46dcd4ef
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

* docs: remove the README section on the version check

The warning already names SRC_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK and links to the
upgrade instructions, and CHANGELOG.md describes the feature.

This reverts commit 71363c82b4753d0859101e940aa446814422821b.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1c29c-9f51-7761-a4ba-4d4f46dcd4ef
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

entry.title: ci: fix build cache, drop duplicated test run (#1385)
entry.content:
ci: fix build cache, drop duplicated test run (#1385)

* ci: cache Go modules and build output per job, drop redundant test pass

Every CI run compiled the whole dependency tree from scratch on all three
OSes, because:

- goreleaser-check ran setup-go without ever building anything, so it
  finished first and saved a 7 KB cache under the key that go-lint and
  go-test on Linux then restored ('cache hit', never re-saved).
- setup-go's built-in cache has no restore-keys, so any go.sum change
  (every renovate PR) started cold on macOS and Windows too.
- go-ci ran 'go test -race' and then 'go test' again, recompiling
  everything without race instrumentation to rerun the same tests.

Now each job owns its cache key (job, OS, arch, Go version, go.sum hash)
with a prefix fallback, goreleaser-check no longer installs Go, and the
test job runs the race pass only.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a18b5c-c5bb-7497-82f1-3e9333c8b7e1
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

* test: run the batch spec upload tests under -race again

The upload tests were tagged //go:build !race in #1082 because testify
fmt-prints every recorded mock argument, and printing a bare
*io.PipeReader reflects into the pipe's internals while the producer
goroutine writes to it. The Windows variant never got the tag, so
'go test -race' has been failing on Windows the whole time, hidden
because the step runs under pwsh, which does not fail on a non-zero
exit in the middle of a multi-line script; the second non-race pass
then went green.

The mock client now wraps the body in a RequestBody struct, so fmt
prints the pointer address instead of walking the pipe. That removes
the need for the !race tag and for the second test pass.

uploadFile also starts the writer goroutine only after NewHTTPRequest
succeeds; before, an error there leaked a goroutine blocked forever on
a pipe nobody reads.

Amp-Thread-ID: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a18b5c-c5bb-7497-82f1-3e9333c8b7e1
Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>

---------

entry.title: help: generate the 'src help' command list from the registered comman…
entry.content:
help: generate the 'src help' command list from the registered commands (#1377)

The "The commands are:" block in 'src help' was a hand-maintained string in
main.go. It had drifted from the registered commands: 'debug', 'snapshot',
and 'lsp' were never added, and the codeowners description differed from
the command's own Usage.

Build the list at runtime from both registries (legacy 'commands' and
urfave/cli 'migratedCommands'). Legacy commands get a 'description' field
and a 'hidden' flag; 'src doc' uses the same flag instead of hard-coding
the names to skip. 'version' gets a Usage so it has a description.

Tests keep the three lists apples-to-apples:
- 'src help' == registered commands (TestHelpListsAllRegisteredCommands)
- 'src doc' root index == 'src help' == registered (TestDocRootIndexMatchesHelp)
- every visible command has a description (TestRootCommandsAreWellFormed)

Co-authored-by: Amp <amp@ampcode.com>
